overview: Black plays 2...b5 straight away, offering the b-pawn Benko-style. After 3.cxb5 Black gets a half-open b-file and a fianchetto, but without the ...c5 setup. It is a rare gambit and the pawn is hard to justify.

white_ideas.idea: Take the pawn and return it with a3, e3 and Nc3
Use the centre with d4 and e4

typical_structures.structure: White centre pawns on c4 and d4

character.notes: The gambit gives open play on the queenside.

gambit.notes: Black gives the b-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: It lacks the ...c5 and ...d6 support of the Benko.

structure.notes: White centre against a Black queenside attack.

character.reason: Black gives a pawn for queenside play, so both sides run risks.

gambit.reason: Black offers the b-pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.reason: White just takes and Black has less compensation than in the Benko.

structure.reason: Black gets a half-open b-file against a White centre.

level.reason: A dubious line is not a first choice.

plans.reason: Black pushes on the queenside with the bishop on b7.
